title: How a silent e changes a word
examples: Why is there an e at the end of cake?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: Look at this little word on the board: cap, like the hat you wear in the sun. Listen to the middle sound, a, short and quick, as in apple. Say it with me: c, a, p.

draw.text: How a silent e changes a word

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: A short a, as in apple

explain.say: Now watch. I add one letter at the end, e. See it light up? It is silent, so you do not say it. But it does a magic trick: it makes the a say its name, ay. Cap becomes cape!

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: See the a glowing now? That is the letter that changed. A long vowel says its own name: a says ay, i says eye, o says oh. Can you hear the difference between cap and cape?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: It works with other vowels too. Here is kite on the board. Without the e it would be kit. With the e, the i says its name, eye. Now you try: hop and hope, cub and cube.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The silent e makes the i say eye

explain.say: Fantastic! On the board, every short word on the left has a twin with a silent e on the right. Challenge: what happens to the word not when you add an e? You get note!

faq.q: What does a silent e do?
faq.a: A silent e at the end of a word is not spoken, but it makes the vowel before it say its name. Cap becomes cape and kit becomes kite.
asks: Why is there an e at the end of cake?

faq.q: What is a long vowel sound?
faq.a: A long vowel says the name of the letter: a in cake, e in Pete, i in bike, o in rope and u in cube.
In cape, the a and the e work together to make one sound, ay, with the p in between. Teachers call that a split digraph.

faq.q: Does a silent e always make the vowel long?
faq.a: Not always. In have, give and love the vowel stays short. These common words are learned by sight.
asks: Why is give not said like five?

faq.q: Was the silent e ever said out loud?
faq.a: Yes. About 600 years ago that final e was spoken. People stopped saying it, but the spelling stayed and became a handy signal for a long vowel.
asks: Why did English keep the silent e?

facts: In Chaucer's English, about 600 years ago, the final e in words like name was spoken.
Adding a silent e can make a new word: hop and hope, cut and cute, pin and pine.

quiz.say: Add a silent e to tub. What new word do you get?
quiz.show: Add a silent e to tub. What new word do you get?
quiz.why: The silent e makes the u say its name: tub becomes tube.

wrong.1: tubby adds by, not a silent e.
wrong.2: tab changes the vowel instead of adding e.

quiz.say: Which word has a long i because of a silent e?
quiz.show: Which word has a long i because of a silent e?
quiz.why: In bike the silent e makes the i say eye.

wrong.0: bit has no e, so the i is short.
wrong.2: give is an exception: its i stays short.
